references.text: The Lord's guidance of Israel in a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire, also mentioned in Exodus 14:24 when He looked down on the Egyptian camp.
The pillar of cloud moves and separates the Israelites from the Egyptians; it is the same pillar of cloud and fire that the Lord uses to confuse the Egyptians.
The Lord looks down from heaven and confuses the enemies with thunder and fire, similar to God's intervention against the Egyptians.
The Lord confuses enemies in battle, just as He confused the Egyptian camp.
The Lord confuses the enemy camp so that they attack each other, resembling the confusion in the Egyptian camp.
The Lord thundered with great noise and confused the Philistines, similar to how the Lord confused the Egyptians.
Describes God's mighty intervention at the Red Sea with clouds, fire, and thunder.
The morning watch is mentioned, the same time reference as in Exodus 14:24.
God spoke to them through the pillar of cloud, referencing God's presence in the pillar of cloud.
The Lord's guidance in a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire was known among the nations.
Retrospective confirmation of the same event: God's use of darkness and confusion against Egypt.
Theological parallel: God's 'spirit of confusion' strikes Egypt both historically and prophetically.
